source_name: Registar stvarnih vlasnika (Beneficial ownership register, within CRPS)
why_relevant: Beneficial-ownership register built into CRPS (operational since Aug 2021, 25% threshold, AML law basis). Exposes who actually controls local POS/IT integrators and bidders — essential for detecting that several 'independent' bidders share an owner, and for group-level competitor mapping.

source_name: CEJN / ESJN – Elektronski sistem javnih nabavki (registered-bidder and contracting-authority registry)
why_relevant: The national e-procurement system. Beyond live notices (other cells' job), it maintains the registry of registered economic operators (ponuđači) and the roster of contracting authorities (naručioci) — i.e. the enumerable buyer and bidder populations for the whole A2 workstream.

source_name: AZZK – Agencija za zaštitu konkurencije: registri dodijeljene državne pomoći i pomoći male vrijednosti
why_relevant: Operates the state-aid register and de-minimis register (aid granter, beneficiary, measure, decision number, sector, amount, date) plus the annual state-aid report. Directly names companies receiving public money — a complementary enumeration of publicly-funded actors alongside procurement awards.

source_name: Poreska uprava / Uprava prihoda i carina – elektronska fiskalizacija programme pages (software-producer registration)
why_relevant: The fiscalisation authority publishes technical/functional specifications, software-development instructions, testing timelines and the procedure by which software producers register — the mechanism that in practice creates the list of fiscalisation-approved POS/ENU vendors, i.e. the terminal supply chain map. Highest-value pointer for this cell if the vendor list is published.

source_name: Vendor self-declaration cluster of Montenegrin fiscalisation software providers (fiskalnakasa.me, v2-bit.me, tiramisuerp.com, e-invoices.online)
why_relevant: In the absence of an openly published approved-vendor register, the vendors who market fiscalisation/POS software in ME self-identify on their own sites. Snowballing these pages reconstructs a de-facto supply-chain map (who integrates with the tax authority, who resells terminals) and yields competitor names for A2 bidder analysis.

source_name: MONSTAT – Statistički biznis registar (Statistical Business Register)
why_relevant: Statistical register covering all active business entities, with methodology and periodic 'Broj i struktura poslovnih subjekata' releases. Gives the denominator (how many firms, by NACE sector and size) for sizing the addressable buyer/vendor population that the individual registers enumerate by name.

source_name: Komisija za tržište kapitala Crne Gore (SCMN) – registri licenciranih subjekata
why_relevant: Capital-market regulator maintaining registers of management companies, investment funds and investment-service licences (including authorised credit institutions). Completes the licensed-financial-actor population beyond banks/PI/EMI; these entities also procure trading, custody and reporting systems.

source_name: CBCG – Državne institucije / korisni linkovi (directory of Montenegrin state institutions)
why_relevant: Curated link directory of Montenegrin state institutions maintained by the central bank. Cheap, authoritative snowball asset for discovering further regulators, agencies and contracting authorities (and hence more tender pages) that generic search misses.

source_name: Privredna komora Crne Gore (Chamber of Economy) – member/association structures
why_relevant: Chamber of Economy organises members into sector boards (odbori/udruženja) including ICT. Membership and board listings surface the local integrator/vendor population that bids on bank and public POS tenders, and the chamber also republishes procurement and state-aid legislation.

source_name: eTenderi.me (Montenegro tender alert service)
why_relevant: Montenegro-specific commercial bid-alert service: SMS/e-mail/push alerts on new notices, procurement-process tracking, competitor win-rate analytics, and a full database of decisions of the State Commission for Control of Public Procurement Procedures. The competitor-analytics and appeals-decision archive are exactly the derived layers a bank/payments vendor needs to see who wins ME banking IT and card-issuance lots.

source_name: TenderiLIVE (Balkan public-procurement application, ME/BA/RS)
why_relevant: Regional subscription platform normalising tender notices across Montenegro, Bosnia-Herzegovina and Serbia into one searchable stream with saved searches and alerts. Cross-border coverage is the key value: a payments vendor bidding in ME usually bids in RS/BA too, and one feed gives comparable notice/award structure across all three.

source_name: eKapija Tenderi (ekapija-tenderi.com) — Montenegro section
why_relevant: The largest regional business-portal tender service: database of tenders from Serbia, Montenegro and BiH plus ~17 further European countries, with a twice-daily working-day bulletin (plus Saturday) covering new notices, all amendments, and concluded-contract notifications. Amendment tracking and award notices are the hardest part to reconstruct from the national portal alone.

source_name: eKapija business portal — Montenegro edition (me.ekapija.com) tender & procurement-plan search
why_relevant: Beyond public notices, eKapija carries private-sector/commercial-company tenders, procurement plans and prior information notices — the private RFP layer no public register in Montenegro publishes. Banks' own vendor RFPs and SOE purchases often surface here first.

source_name: tenderi.hr — Crna Gora section (Croatian sister platform)
why_relevant: Croatian-market bid-alert product with a Montenegro cross-border module; likely the same backend as javne-nabavke.com. Useful mainly as a duplicate-coverage check and for its FAQ, which documents source lists and update cadence (a rare disclosure of aggregator methodology).

source_name: MontenegroTenders.com
why_relevant: English-language Montenegro-only commercial tender database claiming daily harvesting from official procurement portals, government sites, ministries, local authorities, private authorities and newspapers. Value is the newspaper/private-authority layer and English normalisation for non-local analysts; quality claims are unverified and typical of the Indian-operated tender-aggregator family.

source_name: TendersOnTime — Montenegro / Balkans tenders
why_relevant: Global commercial aggregator with a Balkans regional cut (Serbia, Croatia, Bulgaria, Romania, Albania, Montenegro) plus a dedicated EBRD-tenders view — useful as a single cross-checking stream spanning both national portals and IFI procurement, which is exactly where banking-sector modernisation contracts live.

source_name: TendersInfo — Montenegro & Balkan region tenders
why_relevant: Long-running global tender database with Montenegro and Balkan-region country cuts and customised e-mail alerts; claims both government and private tenders. Relevant chiefly as a third redundancy layer and for its historical archive, which often outlives deleted national notices.

source_name: GlobalTenders — Montenegro tenders
why_relevant: Aggregator that states it ingests Montenegrin authority websites, newspapers, journals and magazines and applies AI/ML normalisation and de-duplication. The stated newspaper/journal ingestion is the differentiator worth testing, since low-value or legacy notices still appear in print in ME.

source_name: TendersGo — Montenegro tracking pages
why_relevant: Smaller SEO-driven aggregator publishing Montenegro sector-tracking posts. Low standalone value, but its public posts occasionally name specific contracting authorities and sectors, which is useful for actor-map snowballing without a subscription.

source_name: WBIF — Western Balkans Investment Framework procurements
why_relevant: Regional donor-platform aggregation of tenders and opportunities under WBIF-financed Western Balkans projects, including Montenegro. Bridges EU/IFI grant pipelines to national implementing bodies and is a leading indicator of contracts that will later appear on national portals.

source_name: DevelopmentAid — Montenegro tender search
why_relevant: Subscription aggregator normalising donor and IFI procurement notices (EU, EBRD, WB, UN agencies) by country; the Montenegro location filter gives one cross-donor stream plus organisation and past-award profiles, which supports competitor mapping for consultancy and IT lots.

source_name: UNGM — United Nations Global Marketplace (and UNGM Pro alerts)
why_relevant: Single aggregation point for 30+ UN bodies' procurement notices, filterable by duty station/country; captures UNDP Montenegro and other UN-agency ME purchases (including IT and digitalisation services) that no national or commercial ME aggregator carries. UNGM Pro adds saved searches and a daily digest.

source_name: Balkan Tender Watch (EU-funded regional CSO procurement-monitoring platform)
why_relevant: EU-supported Western Balkans coalition (Montenegro member: MANS; Institute Alternative also active) that has archived analyses, benchmarking tools and monitoring manuals per country since 2012. Its Montenegro document set is a pointer goldmine: it names the contracting authorities, watchdogs, datasets and systemic weaknesses (e.g. unreported post-award contract amendments) that shape how ME procurement data must be interpreted.
